bibliographic.title: Towards an AI Observatory for the Nuclear Sector: A tool for anticipatory governance
bibliographic.citation_apa: Verma, A., & Williams, E. (2025). Towards an AI Observatory for the Nuclear Sector: A tool for anticipatory governance. In Proceedings of STAIGCHI '25. ACM.

methodology.method_family: Conceptual framework and policy-oriented argument drawing on science and technology studies, public policy, and foresight studies
methodology.study_design: Position/conceptual paper proposing an anticipatory governance system and global AI observatory
methodology.technology_context: AI models embedded in nuclear research and work; generative AI in daily practice; ChatOPG; autonomous reactor operation schemas; maintenance planning

eligibility.decision_rationale: The paper strongly addresses anticipatory AI governance in the highly regulated nuclear sector and notes generative AI adoption risks, but the provided text does not center conversational LLM systems or operational conversational governance mechanisms (guardrails, observability, handoff, contestation) required for central evidence in this review.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Metadata extraction appears corrupted in title field; conversational/LLM governance relevance is partial and depends on sections not fully provided in the excerpt.

appraisal.notes: Conceptual ACM short paper (6 pages) arguing for an anticipatory governance system and AI observatory; no empirical sample, data collection, or evaluation of conversational AI governance controls described in the supplied text.

cerqual.explanation: The argument is coherent and sector-relevant for regulated AI governance, but the supplied text offers limited methodological detail and only incidental evidence on generative or conversational AI tools rather than conversational governance in LLM systems.

coding.theme: Anticipatory governance infrastructure for AI in the nuclear sector
coding.subtheme: Global AI observatory as operationalization mechanism

synthesis.main_claim: AI is rapidly embedding in nuclear sector work, but safety, security, and safeguards consequences are not well understood; an anticipatory system of governance and a global AI observatory are needed to steward safe AI adoption.
synthesis.contribution: Proposes contours of a nuclear-sector AI observatory and anticipatory governance approach grounded in STS, public policy, and foresight, with examples of AI use cases and generative AI adoption in industry and academia.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence for anticipatory and institutional AI governance in regulated high-hazard sectors; cite generative AI adoption examples (e.g., ChatOPG) only peripherally for conversational LLM governance, not as primary mechanistic evidence.
